takeaway: The lower greater curvature is supplied by the left and right gastroepiploic arteries. Left from the splenic artery; right from the gastroduodenal. Short gastrics: fundus. Gastric arteries: lesser curvature.

lines.text: A man has an emergency endoscopy for a bleeding gastric ulcer.
The ulcer sits on the lower greater curvature of the stomach.
This area is supplied by the left and right gastroepiploic arteries.
Of the options, the answer is the left gastroepiploic artery, which comes from the splenic artery.
The right gastroepiploic is a terminal branch of the gastroduodenal artery.
The fundus and the upper greater curvature get the short gastric arteries.
And the lesser curvature is supplied by the left and right gastric arteries.
